gloss: to trade; to deal in; to sell

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {商|あきな}っていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to trade; to deal in; to sell
definitions.explanation: To engage in buying and selling goods as a business. A somewhat literary or traditional word for conducting trade.

examples.japanese: {魚|さかな}を{商|あきな}う{店|みせ}だ。
examples.english: It's a shop that deals in fish.

examples.japanese: {代々|だいだい}{呉服|ごふく}を{商|あきな}ってきた{家|いえ}だ。
examples.english: It's a family that has dealt in kimono fabrics for generations.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}、この{通|とお}りでは{多|おお}くの{商人|しょうにん}が{絹|きぬ}や{茶|ちゃ}を{商|あきな}っていた。
examples.english: In the Edo period, many merchants traded in silk and tea along this street.

notes:
A godan verb (う row) meaning to trade or sell goods. More literary and traditional than {売|う}る or {販売|はんばい}する. Often used when describing established businesses, family trades, or historical commerce. Related to the noun {商|あきな}い (trade, business).

ETYMOLOGY:
Derived from {秋|あき}なう, originally referring to the harvest-season trade that took place in autumn. The kanji {商|しょう} (commerce) is used as an ateji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魚|さかな}を{商|あきな}う — to deal in fish
- {呉服|ごふく}を{商|あきな}う — to deal in kimono fabrics
- {酒|さけ}を{商|あきな}う — to deal in sake
- {代々|だいだい}{商|あきな}う — to trade for generations

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {売|う}る — to sell; the everyday word for selling, while {商|あきな}う implies running a trade as an ongoing business
- {商売|しょうばい}する — to do business; more general and modern, while {商|あきな}う has a traditional flavor
